quotes.text: Activity is not character. It's not intent. It's a pattern sitting in a log waiting for context.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the core shift from judging people to reading activity in context.

quotes.text: From the technical side, insider risk management is a signal correlation engine, not a spy tool. It takes many small events, weighs them against context, and raises a flag when the combination crosses a line you chose.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear one-line definition of what the product is and is not.

quotes.text: Every answer points to something the product enforces, not something the company promises. That matters because a promise depends on who's in charge next year. A setting doesn't
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why structural controls beat reassurances in works council negotiations.

quotes.text: The score is a ranking. It tells analysts what to read first. It doesn't say what happened and it doesn't say why. A high score means the pattern is loud. It doesn't mean the person is guilty.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns against treating a risk score as a verdict.

quotes.text: Preventive friction says we noticed you were about to make a mistake and we stepped in before it counted. The first feels like being caught. The second feels like being helped.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames preventive DLP nudges as a trust-building alternative to retroactive discipline.

chapters.title: Why insider risk programs fail on trust
From detecting bad people to risky activity
GDPR, DPIA and the works council

takeaways: Insider Risk Management correlates activity signals in context; a risk score ranks patterns for review and never proves intent.
Legal basis, DPIA, works council agreement and a split role model with pseudonymization should be settled before any policy goes live.
Start with a small, quiet pilot, tune noise on a fixed cadence with a change log, and tell staff plainly what is and is not monitored.
hook: Most insider risk programs die not because of the tool but because employees find out by rumor. This episode walks security, compliance and HR teams through setting up Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management with pseudonymization, works council involvement, careful triage and honest communication, so the program protects data without alienating staff.
